source.title: Surge Phenomenon in Optimal Learning Rate and Batch Size Scaling
source.authors: Shuai-Peng Li; Peng-Hao Zhao; Hailin Zhang; Xing-Wu Sun; Hao Wu; Dian Jiao; Wei-Yan Wang; Cheng-Jun Liu; Zheng Fang; Jinbao Xue; Yangyu Tao; Bin Cui; Di Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices and checklist.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies optimal learning-rate scaling with batch size and reports loss-improvement results. It does not test whether networks reach near-zero classification error, whether width or depth changes training error, or whether training recovers from learning rates above a stability limit.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern optimal learning rates and loss decrease across batch sizes, not the training-classification-error behavior in the versions. Third-party results in Figure 7 are cited analyses and are not recorded as this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study tests how Adam's optimal learning rate varies with batch size, not any listed claim version. It reports neither stability-threshold crossings, loss surges and recovery, nor sharpness trajectories for V5. Its discussion of edge-of-stability work is a cited limitation of its quadratic approximation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that Adam-style optimal learning rates initially rise and then fall with batch size, that the peak marks a training-speed/data-efficiency trade-off, and that their experiments support the theory. Their fuller account also predicts a nonzero asymptote at very large batch sizes and a peak shifting toward larger batches during training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper investigates optimal learning-rate and batch-size scaling with Adam-style optimizers; it does not use the interventions or outcome measures in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curves vary with workload, batch size, training progress, and Adam configuration; the paper notes that optimizer, weight decay, and gradient clipping may also affect learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the tested workloads, selected Adam learning rates show a declining interval as batch size increases. CNN experiments also show large-batch saturation; ResNet18 experiments show the estimated peak shifting toward larger batches as training loss falls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam's optimal learning rate can vary nonmonotonically with batch size, with a peak whose batch-size location increases during training and a nonzero large-batch asymptote.

record.problems: The experimental evidence is presented mainly in figures without textual numerical learning-rate values. The authors state that their theory uses a quadratic loss approximation and acknowledge that such approximations may not capture large-learning-rate scenarios. They also note that other training factors, including optimizer choice, weight decay, and gradient clipping, are outside the paper's scope.
record.rows_left_out: No results were left out. Figure 7 analyzes third-party results from the DeepSeek paper, so it is not recorded as a result generated by this study.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels, and dependence on size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by residual shortcuts or special training recipes.
Effects of initialization on signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, divergence boundaries and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Optimal learning rates are grid-search selections used to evaluate a separate scaling claim, not evidence of the six versions. The quadratic-approximation caveat supplies no new test or specific refutation of V5. Figure 7 uses third-party results and was already declared excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious minima and student width in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth, identity shortcuts, special initialization, and normalization effects on training error.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.
Stability-limit learning rates, loss surges and recovery, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: 5-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Grid search over learning rates and batch sizes; report optimal learning rate associated with greatest training-loss reduction.
rows.measure: Optimal learning rate as batch size varies; the text reports a decreasing range at small batch sizes and saturation at large batch sizes.
rows.value: Text describes declining range at small batch sizes and saturation at large batch sizes; precise values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend across batch sizes, but gives no textual numerical learning-rate values for this result.
rows.check: The scaling result does not measure a listed version. Table 1 lists both CNN searches with Adam β1=0.9, β2=0.999; their distinction is batch-size range, not optimizer configuration. Figures 2(b) and 2(c) describe small- and large-batch regimes.

rows.subject: 5-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Grid search over learning rates and batch sizes; report optimal learning rate associated with greatest training-loss reduction.
rows.measure: Optimal learning rate as batch size varies; the text reports a decreasing range at small batch sizes and saturation at large batch sizes.
rows.value: Text describes declining range at small batch sizes and saturation at large batch sizes; precise values are figure only.
rows.note: Table 1 lists two CNN configurations; the paper does not separately describe which configuration maps to the plotted result, so the result is not assigned to one configuration.
rows.check: Unsupported CNN condition: Table 1 lists no CNN experiment with β1=β2=0. Correct to β1=0.9, β2=0.999 and distinguish the large-batch search from the small-batch search, or merge with R1. The current row duplicates the same textual result under an incorrect configuration.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Grid search over learning rates and batch sizes at several training-loss levels.
rows.measure: Optimal learning rate as batch size varies; the text says rates primarily trend downward after batch size exceeds estimated Bnoise.
rows.value: Text reports a primarily downward trend after batch size exceeds estimated Bnoise; precise values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Training-loss levels are captioned with ± 0.001; uncertainty for the learning-rate trend is not stated.
rows.note: The six training-loss levels are reported separately in the figure caption; the text describes the overall trend across the plotted settings.
rows.check: Adam configuration is wrong: Table 1 lists ResNet18 with β1=0.0, β2=0.0. The ±0.001 values specify achieved training-loss levels, not uncertainty in optimal learning rates. Neither the loss levels nor the scaling trend measures a listed version.

rows.check: The configuration matches Figure 4(a), but the selected learning rates and subsequent loss decreases do not establish any listed version.
